examples.purpose: A PIN pad, the guide's Content PIN and its Do “Shuffle for a PIN”: masked dots above a Numpad with shuffle left on (the default) and no decimal key. “● ● ○ ○” stands for a four-digit PIN with two digits typed; onKeyPress stands for the screen updating the PIN and its dots on each key press.

from.quote: or masked dots for a PIN, never the PIN itself.

examples.purpose: Adding money to a wallet, the guide's In context, before any amount is typed: a Card holding a VStack with the text “Add money”, a shuffled Numpad with its decimal key, and the screen's Button, disabled and reading “Enter an amount” until there is an amount. onKeyPress stands for the screen updating the amount on each key press, and onPress for adding the money. The guide shows the amount (₹0) between the text and the pad in a MoneyValue, which has no entry in this pack, so it is left out: report that the amount needs MoneyValue.

props.description: When true, digit positions (0-9) are randomised on each mount for anti-keylogging / shoulder-surfing protection. The decimal and backspace keys keep their fixed positions. Default true, from the component source.

gaps.text: Figma shows the keys in 1–9 order with a “←” glyph; the package shuffles the digits by default and draws a backspace icon.
Figma's Numpad is 318 × 245, with 98 × 52.25 keys; the package's keys are at least 46 px tall, and at 318 px wide it measures 318 × 220, with 98 × 46 keys.
